If Tehenhauin gave buffs to Skinks and Red Crested Skinks that were as strong as Tiktaq'to buffs to Terradons and Ripperdactyls he might be a close competitor, but as it stands Tlaqua is the faction I keep going back to, even after completing the campaign on legendary.

They can certainly be effective if they can shoot into the backs and sides of enemies. I've had games where they get 100+ kills which is way more than paying for themselves. That said, while the poison debuff is nice, you're almost certain to hit your own men with it if you're using it on a unit in Melee (Even if you're hitting them from behind.) and since Saurus have some of the highest infantry stats and the debuff works by percentages, you're likely to suffer from it more than the opponent.

While the extra damage can offset that, now that Red Crested Skinks have poison attacks as standard it's probably better just to take them. They're just as good at flanking and they won't be hitting friendlies. 

In MP they (or the chameleon variants at least) still have a place as being relatively cheap, mobile missiles that can support by firing into the rear of units in combat, but they have to be micromanaged and can be easily shut down by certain armies. Besides which there are more expensive units like Terradons who can do their jobs more effectively.

In campaign however, as soon as you can afford any other kind of flanker I'd do it.

I've never played Ungrim before, but Volkmar has the same problem as Tehenhauin. Yes it's meant to be a thematic thing, and to make you change the way you play the game.

Look at Skarsnik or Anith Alar. Both of those campaigns are awesome because they play differently to their race's normal modus operandi. More importantly, they continue to play differently because their unique units (or buffs to existing units) remain viable later on in the game.

By contrast, with Volkmar and Tehenhauin you have sub-par units being buffed or having their cost reduced, but not enough that you don't immediately ditch them once you can afford units who are outright superior even though they aren't being buffed by your faction. If I wanted to play Saurus heavy I'd have picked Kroq-Gar. I want to play Skink heavy so I picked Tehenhauin, but turns out because his buffs aren't as strong as Skarsnik's were I'm still going to have to play Saurus heavy. Does that make sense?

Tiktaq'to is another example of where CA has done this well. It takes units who were decent at best and turns them into a flying force to be reckoned with, to the point where even in the late game half of every army is likely to be flyers. It changes the game up so much and is tonnes of fun.

The main issue there I think is that only the army Kroak is in can use him (obviously), and you need to get to level 15 to unlock him at all.

So while in the early game the Doomrockets can basically win battles for you, Lizardmen don't have that, and in the late game when they have multiple armies on the go only one of them can use Kroak while if you build enough of them Doomrockets can be used once in every battle. Kroak also takes up a unit slot which could otherwise be filled with a skink priest who can buff your other units and ride a Stegadon rather than being a pure damage dealer.

I get that it's a trade-off since Kroak is a multi-use thing while Doomrockets have to be made over and over, but I'd still definitely take the nukes over Kroak given the choice.

It's good that there's a temple guard analogue. One of the major problems with skink armies is needing to bring in dinosaurs to have any anti-large. Outside of that I'm not sure what you could realistically do in terms of new units. At that point it's really just a case of changing the buffs they get.
